discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Feynman proposed using one quantum system to emulate another. Jaksch and Zoller's 1998 proposal showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, the first clean realization of a strongly correlated lattice model with neutral atoms. Building on this, Greiner and Bloch developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution, imaging Mott shells, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, and many-body localization dynamics. Zoller's theoretical framework, together with these experiments, established analog quantum simulation as a new experimental method for problems in condensed-matter physics that computation cannot settle, including high-temperature superconductivity and disorder-interaction physics. It underpins a worldwide field and today's neutral-atom quantum processors. This is a discovery in quantum many-body physics with broad impact on fundamental science and technology.
